- Close-up of a soybean stem at a node
- Green stem (plant still alive)
- Gray/white fluffy/cottony growth at the node junction
- Surrounding leaves are yellowing
- The fluffy gray-white mass at node is prominent

This strongly suggests White_Mold or possibly Green_stem_disorder. Let me check reference images.
White_Mold reference shows fluffy white cottony growth at nodes on green stems — very similar to test image. Let me also check Diaporthe and Sudden_death_syndrome for comparison.
Diaporthe shows dark brown stems, SDS shows leaf necrosis — neither matches. Let me view two more for thoroughness.

The evidence is clear. The test image shows:
- A green soybean stem at a node
- **Gray/white fluffy cottony mass** at the node junction — characteristic Sclerotinia mycelium
- Yellowing surrounding leaves (plant approaching maturity while infected)

This matches White_Mold precisely: the White_Mold reference images show the same fluffy white/gray cottony growth at nodes on green stems. Phomopsis/Diaporthe show pod/seed lesions, Charcoal_Rot shows dried gray stems with black specks, and Green_stem_disorder has no fungal growth — none match the cottony node growth seen here.
